speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear you're dealing with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms, and did they start at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP. Can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions and whether they are itchy or painful? Please also detail any specific sexual practices you had during your return from Minnesota.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Skin Lesions: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm. Sexual Practices: Not recorded in the provided measurement data.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme arthritis with secondary reactive arthritis or disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI). Given the history of recent camping in Minnesota, knee pain, and wrist monoarthritis, Lyme disease is the primary concern; however, the sexually active status and potential rash require ruling out DGI. I request images of the skin lesions and the wrist joint for further confirmation.
